children.objective: Explore cooperative staging of source-particle positions and masses into shared memory so each source tile is reused by multiple output particles. Focus on tile loading, synchronization, tail handling, and shared-memory/occupancy tradeoffs; keep the pairwise arithmetic and output strategy otherwise close to the baseline, and retain the default launch geometry unless the tile requires a change. Respect the 49152-byte shared-memory limit and ensure every output is written exactly once for every N. Evaluate only programs that pass the full correctness suite and compare the official geometric-mean timing across N=4096, 8192, and 16384 under the prescribed search protocol.
children.subject: Shared-memory tiling for source-particle reuse

children.objective: Explore register blocking by assigning each thread a small group of output particles and maintaining separate target states and force accumulators while streaming source particles. Do not add shared-memory source tiling or change the force formula, so this tests a distinct reuse strategy. Experiment with mappings that preserve efficient input/output access and control register pressure; handle partial groups and all legal N so every output is produced exactly once. Record correctness, configuration, and official geometric-mean timings under the prescribed search protocol.
children.subject: Register-blocked multiple outputs per thread

children.objective: Explore pairwise arithmetic changes while keeping the baseline one-output-per-thread mapping and global-memory strategy as close as practical. Measure explicit rsqrtf-based formulations and the algebraic cancellation of target mass when computing acceleration; optionally test eliminating the self-interaction branch only when the softened self term remains well-defined. Do not enable global fast math or specialize to benchmark inputs. Preserve G=1, softening=0.001f, update order, exact masses, and required float32 behavior; reject any candidate that fails the independent oracle or any required case, including coincident positions, extreme isolated mass, and zero or negative dt.
children.subject: Pairwise arithmetic and numerical-accuracy tradeoffs

children.objective: Explore legal block and items_per_block configurations and the corresponding output-index mapping using a baseline-style one-output-per-thread kernel, without shared-memory tiling or register blocking. Ensure the mapping honors grid.x=ceil(N/items_per_block), covers every output exactly once even when the two values differ, and handles tails for all N. Keep shared_memory_bytes zero unless required by the unchanged kernel. Compare correct candidates by the prescribed geometric-mean kernel time, not by a single size.

decision.rationale: Inspect the fastest correct measured candidate's actual kernel before deciding what to integrate. T1 is valid/correct at 0.00113314 s versus the valid baseline at 0.00185035 s; T2 is slower, T3 is incorrect, and T4 is approximately baseline. I will not infer compatibility or combine ideas without inspecting source.

Use the fastest measured correct candidate unchanged for this integration round: its shared-memory-tiled kernel passed correctness and measured 0.00113314 s versus the baseline's 0.00185035 s. Its source preserves ascending pair order and handles inactive tail threads across barriers. Recompile and check it afresh as required. Do not add arithmetic changes: T3 failed correctness. T2 was substantially slower standalone, so retain that branch for possible later combination rather than treating it as a verified improvement.

The 512-tile integration is valid and currently best at 0.00112490 s, but only marginally ahead of the 256-tile candidate. T2's two-output-per-thread candidate was slower alone; inspect its source before deciding whether that distinct reuse strategy is compatible and worth one combination attempt with the shared-memory base.

Try one complementary combination: retain the valid 512-source shared-memory base (0.00112490 s) and add T2's two-output-per-thread mapping, which was correct but slow standalone (0.00274554 s). The shared tile could feed both targets per thread and amortize source staging, though higher register use and fewer CTAs may lose. Use block=256, items_per_block=512, shared_memory_bytes=0; ensure every thread reaches both tile barriers, including inactive tail threads, and preserve each target's ascending source accumulation and update order. Recheck the full suite and measure afresh; keep the current base if the combination fails or regresses.
